You request a direct intercession from the natural world. Nature always refuses unnatural requests and might grant a different request (potentially more powerful or better fitting its character) than the one you asked for. A primal phenomenon spell can do any of the following things.

• Duplicate any spell from the primal spell list of 9th rank or lower to which you have access.

• Duplicate any spell from another spell list of 7th rank or lower. It must be common or you must have access.

• Produce any effect whose power level is in line with the above effects.

• Reverse certain effects that refer to the Wish spell.

At the GM's discretion, you can try to use primal phenomenon to produce greater effects than these, but doing so may be dangerous, or the spell may have only a partial effect.

raga-of-remembrance.fuente: Pathfinder Lost Omens Monsters of Myth
raga-of-remembrance.descripcion:
You scribe occult symbols on unblighted Vudran ground, laying the ceramics within them to create a ritual space. To perform the ritual, light incense in the ceramics and sit at the center of the ritual space. You then play the disharmonic instrument, drawing on musical skill, occult harmonics, or religious tradition. This establishes an underlying drone atop which the secondary casters layer their own performances. The song calls to the millions who died defending Vudra from Kothogaz, investing their power in Vanitapati, the legendary psychic.

—

Critical Success A towering, ethereal avatar of Vanitapati manifests around you, surrounded by swirling spirits. The avatar weakens Kothogaz's spirit. While Kothogaz is within 1 mile of you, it is Frightened 2 and is permanently destroyed if reduced to 0 Hit Points.

Success As critical success, but Kothogaz is Frightened 1.

Failure The dead come to your aid, but their presence is unnerving. As success, but Kothogaz isn't frightened, and the primary and secondary casters take a -1 status penalty to saving throws against emotion effects.

Critical Failure Rather than the dead, Kothogaz hears the ritual's call and immediately teleports to the primary caster with its Disharmonic Door ability. Primary and secondary casters are afflicted with many-eyed blight.

remake.descripcion:
You fully re-create an object from nothing, even if the object was destroyed. To do so, you must be able to picture the object in your mind. Additionally, the material component must be a remnant of the item, no matter how small or insignificant (even a speck of dust that remains from Disintegrate is enough). The spell fails if your imagination relied on too much guesswork; if the object would be too large to fit in a 5-foot cube; if the object still exists and you were simply not aware of it; or if the object is an artifact, has a level over 20, or has similar vast magical power.

The item reassembles in perfect condition. Even if your mental image was of a damaged or weathered object, the new one is in this perfected form. If the object was magical, this spell typically restores its constant magical properties, but not any temporary ones, such as charges or one-time uses. An item with charges or uses per day has all of its uses expended when remade, but it replenishes them normally thereafter.

revival.descripcion:
A burst of healing energy soothes living creatures and temporarily rouses those recently slain. All living targets regain 10d8+40 Hit Points.

In addition, you return any number of dead targets to life temporarily, with the same effects and limitations as Raise Dead. The raised creatures have a number of temporary Hit Points equal to the Hit Points you gave living creatures, but no normal Hit Points. The raised creatures can't regain Hit Points or gain temporary Hit Points in other ways, and once revival's duration ends, they lose all temporary Hit Points and die.

Revival can't resurrect creatures killed by Disintegrate or a death effect. It has no effect on undead.
revival.objetivos: dead creatures and living creatures of your choice within range

shadow-army.descripcion:
You create dozens of semi-real copies of yourself that swarm across the battlefield and fight your enemies. You're virtually indistinguishable from your clones, allowing you to  and  among them. An enemy that's in the area when the spell is cast or that ends their turn in the area takes 3d10 mental damage and 3d10 bludgeoning damage, and is possibly inflicted with a condition, depending on the result of their Will save. When you Cast the Spell, you choose a condition your shadows impose on a failed save: Clumsy 2, Enfeebled 2, Off-Guard, or Slowed 1.

—
Critical Success The creature takes no damage. For the duration of the spell, the creature uses the outcome one degree of success better than it rolled on further saves against the spell and can distinguish you from your clones without difficulty.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and gains the chosen condition until the end of its next turn.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and gains the chosen condition until the end of its next turn.

song-of-the-fallen.descripcion:
You chant a dirge or an elegy that either rouses the dead to action or reminds undead that they should lay to rest.

If you target dead creatures, the bodies animate and can continue acting as if they were alive. A creature animated in this way has 60 temporary Hit Points. The animated creatures are Slowed 1 but can otherwise act normally. Creatures animated with this spell die again once the spell ends.

If you target undead creatures, each undead must attempt a basic Will save.

—
Critical Success The undead takes 5d6 vitality damage.

Success The undead takes 10d6 vitality damage and is slowed 1 for 1 round.

Failure The undead takes 100 vitality damage and is slowed 1 for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The undead is destroyed.
song-of-the-fallen.objetivos: up to 4 dead creatures or up to 4 undead creatures

summon-oliphaunt-of-jandelay.descripcion:
You briefly summon the mythical Oliphaunt of Jandelay, unleashing a manifestation of pure destruction that obliterates everything unfortunate enough to stand in its path. The summoned Oliphaunt occupies the space of a Gargantuan creature. It has a Speed of 200 feet.

Arrive (force) Devastating Displacement Using hidden magics and long-lost techniques, you conjure an immense gate to Jandelay, compelling the Oliphaunt to step through. The Oliphaunt arrives in a 60-foot burst. Each creature in the area takes 8d10 force damage (basic Reflex save). On a failure, the creature is also pushed 60 feet away from the Oliphaunt.

Depart Annihilating Trample The Oliphaunt becomes aware that it has been summoned to a world that isn't on the verge of annihilation. It summons another enormous gate to Jandelay 200 feet in front of it. The Oliphaunt then rages forward through the gate, crushing everything in its path, before closing the gate behind it and disappearing. The Oliphaunt creates an 80-foot-wide path of devastation that extends 200 feet. Each creature and vehicle in the area takes 8d8 bludgeoning damage (basic Fortitude save). A creature or vehicle reduced to 0 Hit Points is smashed into fine powder; its gear, passengers, and cargo remain. An unattended object in the area is destroyed unless it succeeds at a Fortitude save, regardless of Hardness, or unless it's an artifact or similarly hard to destroy. This trample automatically destroys any force effect, such as a wall of force.
summon-oliphaunt-of-jandelay.duracion: until the end of your next turn

synchronize-ley-line.descripcion:
Secondary Casters (continued) 2–4

—
You attempt to synchronize one of the vaultlines with either Life or Death. The skills used by the primary caster, as well as a unique symbolic action that must be performed to calm the line, vary according to which line is being synchronized and whether it's being synchronized with Life or Death.

If the primary caster fails but doesn't critically fail their skill check, all casters suffer the vaultline's backlash effect, but the line is successfully synchronized. On a critical failure, the backlash effect occurs, and the ritual must be attempted again. On a critical success, the line is synchronized, and the DC of any check the primary caster makes to perform the synchronize ley line ritual in the next 24 hours is reduced by 1.

—
Empathic (Life): The primary caster shares a vivid memory of joy or love, attempting a Diplomacy DC 45 or Performance DC 45 check.

Empathic (Death): The primary caster admits to a secret grudge or resentment, attempting a Intimidation DC 45 or Society DC 45 check.

Secondary Checks Speak encouraging words to soothe the emotional tempest around the line (Diplomacy DC 38), pit your own rage, hate, or fear against surging negative energies (Intimidation DC 37), use music, poetry, or dance to raise your allies' spirits (Performance DC 39).

Backlash Each caster takes a –2 circumstance penalty to their next saving throw against a spell or effect with the emotion trait within the next 24 hours.

—
Entropic (Life): The primary caster recounts a personal experience of confronting something alien or unknowable, attempting a Arcana DC 45 or Occultism DC 45 check.

Entropic (Death): The primary caster describes a moment of feeling lost or disconnected, attempting a Deception DC 45 or Occultism DC 45 check.

Secondary Checks Embrace the silence of the void (Stealth DC 37), empty your mind to vanish from the psychic mindscape (Deception DC 36), offer a prayer to deities of nothingness (Religion DC 38)

Backlash Each caster takes 3d6 void damage (basic Fortitude DC 40 save).

—
Mephitic (Life): The primary caster offers a heartfelt vow to protect an ally and performs a symbolic (or literal) act of healing on them, attempting a Medicine DC 45 or Nature DC 45 check.

Mephitic (Death): The primary caster describes a personal experience of physical or spiritual harm, attempting a Religion DC 45 or Survival DC 45 check.

Secondary Checks Absorb the vaultline's toxic energies (Survival DC 37), tend to ailments affecting nearby NPCs or the environment (Medicine DC 36), identify and neutralize individual toxins afflicting the line (Crafting DC 36 or Alchemy Lore)

Backlash Each caster takes 3d6 poison damage (basic Fortitude DC 40 save).

—
Noetic (Life): The primary caster recounts a personal experience or realization that changed their outlook, attempting a Arcana DC 45 or Society DC 45 check.

Noetic (Death): The primary caster willingly abandons a long-held misconception or prejudice aloud, attempting a Deception DC 45 or Intimidation DC 45 check.

Secondary Checks Interpret patterns pulsing through the ley currents (Arcana DC 37), project a positive outlook to ward off psychic backlash (Diplomacy DC 36), use calming chants and rhythms to steady the magic's flow (Performance DC 38).

Backlash Each caster takes 3d6 mental damage (basic Will DC 40 save).

—
Recalescent (Life): The primary caster makes a passionate declaration of hope or courage and symbolically ignites a flame to accompany it, attempting a Nature DC 45 or Religion DC 45 check.

Recalescent (Death): The primary caster douses a flame to symbolically extinguish an ambition or desire, attempting a Nature DC 45 or Occultism DC 45 check.

Secondary Checks Construct sacred bonfires (Crafting DC 37), chant incantations or drum mystical rhythms to empower the flames (Performance DC 38), stoke fires to keep them burning (Athletics DC 36)

Backlash Each caster takes 3d6 fire damage (basic Reflex DC 40 save).

—
Temporal (Life): The primary caster describes or reenacts a new beginning or symbolic rebirth, attempting a Diplomacy DC 45 or Performance DC 45 check.

Temporal (Death): The primary caster delivers a eulogy for a fallen loved one or recounts an experience of tragic loss, attempting a Intimidation DC 45 or Religion DC 45 check.

Secondary Checks Recall historical accounts and legends intersecting with the vaultline's trajectory through time (Society DC 38 or relevant Lore), detect and identify chronological distortions in the area (Perception DC 37), perfectly time your movements to sync your existence with the line's temporal pulses (Performance DC 39)

Backlash Each caster takes a –2 circumstance penalty on their next saving throw against a spell or effect with the time trait within the next 24 hours.

tear-the-veil.descripcion:
You cause the barrier between the Universe and the Void to weaken as waves of void energy pull the living toward the tear to their inevitable doom. The area is difficult terrain to all living creatures. When you Cast this Spell and the first time each round you Sustain it on subsequent rounds, all living creatures in the area must attempt a Fortitude saving throw.

—
Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes 5d12 void damage and is pulled 15 feet toward the center.

Failure The target takes 10d12 void damage and is pulled 30 feet toward the center.

Critical Failure The target takes 20d12 void damage and is pulled 30 feet toward the center.

There's an additional 5-foot burst in the center of the area that drains the life away from all who touch it. Whenever a living creature begins its turn in this burst, it becomes Drained 1, or its drained condition increases by 1 to a maximum of Drained 4. A target that is drained 4 and begins its turn in the center burst must attempt a Fortitude save that has the death and incapacitation traits; on a failure, it is reduced to 0 Hit Points, crumbles into ash, and becomes a wraith. The gear of the creature that's transformed in this way falls to the ground in its space.

theogeny.descripcion: You spark the genesis of a new divine realm around you. The appearance of the area becomes more obviously divine, matching your own beliefs. All creatures within the area temporarily transcend into divine beings. If you're holy, your allies gain the holy trait, while your foes gain the unholy trait and weakness 5 to holy. Similarly, if you're unholy, your allies gain the unholy trait, while your foes gain the holy trait and weakness 5 to unholy. Creatures that already have the holy or unholy trait don't gain any new traits or weaknesses. While in the area, you and all allies gain a fly Speed equal to their highest Speed, and their Strikes gain the sanctified trait and deal an additional 1d10 spirit damage on hit. Additionally, all enemies take 10 spirit damage whenever they're critically hit by an attack or whenever they critically fail a saving throw.

veil-of-broken-reality.descripcion:
Area 100-mile burst

You conceal reality, letting time proceed, though none perceive it. Whenever a creature enters the area or starts its turn in the area, the creature must attempt a Will saving throw. A creature of 16th level or lower automatically critically fails. You can designate up to 10 creatures to be immune from this part of the spell. Regardless of the result, the creature becomes temporarily immune for the remainder of the duration.

When this spell ends, all events that took place within the area are wiped from the memories of all creatures everywhere (including yourself and other excluded creatures), all records of the events are erased, and all attempts to receive any information about the events are automatically negated. Only an impossible spell specifically crafted for seeing a particular event can retrieve any knowledge of the events that took place.

—
Critical Success The creature automatically learns you're the spell's caster, your current location, and the effect of the spell.

Success The creature is Slowed 1 and knows you're the spell's caster.

Failure The creature is slowed 1 and can't use reactions.

Critical Failure The creature is Slowed 3 and can't use reactions. When you Fuel Veil of Broken Reality, you cast freeze time without expending a spell slot.

—
Lethologic Mark You become unremarkable in presence and sometimes slip outside of reality altogether. Those you meet forget your name and identity 1 hour after they leave your presence. Those who already knew you must succeed at a Flat DC 5 each morning; on a failure, they forget you and your identity until the next morning. If they forget you 3 days in a row, the effect lasts until the lethologic mark is removed. To heal this mark, you—or those willing to assist you—must learn and speak five of your true names successively, knowledge that has been scattered to the far corners of the Dimension of Time.

wish.descripcion:
You weave the fabric of reality itself to grant the target's greatest desire. The target declares their wish in a loud voice at the start of the ritual and again at the end. The target's wish can be anything, ranging from simpler wishes such as vast riches or the casting of a certain spell or ritual, to greater wishes like the destruction of an entire kingdom or ascension to divinity. The GM might decide a wish draws the attention of deities or other powerful creatures, leading to interference with the ritual or attempts to undo the wish. The power of the ritual alters reality to such a degree that even deities can't outright undo the wish, but they can react to the wish by sending servitors to take away the newly acquired riches, for example.

—

Critical Success The wish is granted without complication or drawbacks.

Success The wish is granted, but with unintended consequences or side effects, such as taking riches from a well-known criminal, stirring a damaged kingdom to war, or angering rival gods.

Failure The wish fails and has no result. The GM can instead have the wish be partially granted, but to such a lesser degree that the target will be eternally unsatisfied.

Critical Failure The wish is corrupted, resulting in a cruel fulfillment. The GM determines the full results, but the outcome is generally ironic in some nature, such as becoming trapped in an underground vault full of riches, being transported to the kingdom as it's destroyed, or achieving divinity within an inaccessible demiplane.
